newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLAMES BEAT OILERS IN OVERTIME.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLAMES BEAT OILERS IN OVERTIME.

text.p: Robert Reichel scored a power-play goal 2:20 into overtime to lift the Calgary Flames to their season-high fourth straight win, 3-2 over the archrival Edmonton Oilers Thursday.

Edmonton winger Andrei Kovalenko was called for tripping Reichel in the Oilers' zone 52 seconds into overtime, setting up a Calgary power play. From the high slot, Reichel stopped Tommy Albelin's pass and blasted a waist-high slap shot through traffic and past goaltender Bob Essensa.
"In the last five games I'm a much different hockey player, I have confidence," Reichel said. "I'm much better."
"There was electricity here tonight, sometimes you can feel it," Calgary's Corey Millen said. "We started off slow but we took advantage of the opportunity at the end and it's a big win for us."
Dave Gagner and Aaron Gavey also scored for Calgary, which has won the first four games of a five-game homestand. The Flames are 2-3 against the Oilers this season.
Ryan Smyth and Miroslav Satan tallied for Edmonton, which suffered just its second loss in eight games.
In Philadelphia, Mikael Renberg and Joel Otto scored 2:13 apart in the third period and Garth Snow extended his personal unbeaten streak to 10 games as the Flyers defeated the Ottawa Senators 4-2.

The Flyers had some anxious moments in the second period when superstar Eric Lindros was hit by Ottawa's Janne Laukkanen and suffered an apparent left knee injury. But he returned before the period ended.

John LeClair set up both third-period goals for Philadelphia, which has won six straight over the Senators. The Flyers moved back into first place in the Atlantic Division with 70 points, one ahead of idle Florida.
In St Louis, Grant Fuhr turned aside 32 shots and Scott Pellerin, Brett Hull and Jim Campbell scored second-period goals, leading the Blues to a 4-1 victory over the New York Rangers.
Pierre Turgeon had a goal and an assist and Craig Conroy set up a pair of scores for St Louis, 2-2-2 in its last six games.
Brian Leetch scored the lone goal for New York, which has lost two of three on a four-game road trip that concludes Saturday in Chicago.
New York's Wayne Gretzky, who played 18 games with the Blues last season, was booed each time he touched the puck. He has now gone 18 games without a goal.
At Los Angeles, Jan Vopat scored with 8:06 left in the third period as the Kings returned home and stopped a three-game losing streak with a 4-4 tie against the Toronto Maple Leafs.
Vopat took a pass from Sean O'Donnell inside the blue line and released a slap shot that hit goaltender Felix Potvin's left pad before trickling over the goal line.
Sean O'Donnell had a goal and two assists for the Kings, who went 3-0-1 against the Maple Leafs this season. Los Angeles had a season-high 55 shots while holding Toronto to 30.
Potvin made 51 saves for the Maple Leafs, who are just 2-5-2 in their last nine games.
In Chicago, Gary Suter broke out of a prolonged slump with two goals and two assists and the surging Blackhawks set a season high for scoring in a 7-3 rout of the San Jose Sharks.
Former Sharks Michal Sykora and Ulf Dahlen were among four Blackhawks with a goal and an assist apiece as Chicago won for the fifth time in six games.
Chris Terreri, acquired with Sykora and Dahlen in a trade three weeks ago for goaltender Ed Belfour, stopped 22 shots and beat his former team for the second time in two meetings.

In New Jersey, Martin Brodeur made 20 saves for his fifth shutout of the season and Brian Rolston scored twice as the Devils extended their NHL-best unbeaten streak to nine games with a 4-0 victory over the Hartford Whalers.
Brodeur stopped five shots in the first period, six in the second and nine in the third en route to his 17th career shutout. He is 7-0-3 in his last 10 games.
In Phoenix, Sandis Ozolinsh scored twice and Valeri Kamensky had a goal and an assist to lead the Colorado Avalanche to a 3-2 victory over the Coyotes.

Ozolinsh has four of his 18 goals against the Coyotes, helping Colorado outscore Phoenix 13-3 in winning all three meetings this season. The Avalanche have won six of the last seven meetings with the Coyotes.
Keith Tkachuk scored on a two-man advantage and added another goal for the Coyotes, who had won three of their previous four games.
